newsitem.title: MEXICO: Production of premium tequila doubles - industry.
newsitem.headline: Production of premium tequila doubles - industry.

text.p: Production of 100 percent pure agave tequila, the premium drink that is becoming fashionable in up-market restaurants in Mexico and abroad, doubled in the first 10 months of the year compared with the same period in 1995, industry figures showed.
Ouput of blended tequila, the cheaper brand often used for margaritas and other cocktails, also increased, but at a lower rate, the Tequila Regulatory Council said in an internal report.
It said Mexico produced 17.1 million liters of 100 percent agave tequila in the 10 months to October, compared with 8.5 million liters during the same period in 1995.
Some 62.3 million liters of blended tequila were produced, 15.96 percent above the 52.8 million liters of the year before.
Exports of quality tequila also soared 74.24 percent between January and October, while those of its blended counterparts were up 14 percent.

Though only 11.6 percent of tequila exports are bottled, the rest being carried in tequila tankers, the amount of bottled tequila sold abroad jumped 37 percent in the first 10 months of the year, the council said.
It said the United States was the principal export market, followed by Holland, Belgium, Germany, France and Japan.
